mainEntity.name: What is a Salesforce data migration?

acceptedAnswer.text: A data migration moves records from an existing system into Salesforce through five stages: data extraction, field mapping, data cleaning, sandbox test loading, and production loading with validation. Timelines vary by volume: under 10,000 records takes 1-2 weeks, 10,000 to 100,000 takes 3-5 weeks, over 100,000 takes 6-8 weeks including testing.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my Salesforce org needs an audit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Five signs indicate an audit is overdue: reports show data leadership questions, automations fire unexpectedly, new hires take over two weeks to learn the system, nobody can explain what specific automations do, or you have 20+ custom objects with no data dictionary. An org audit reviews data quality, automation health, security model, technical debt, and documentation gaps.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between Salesforce Flows and Process Builder?

acceptedAnswer.text: Process Builder is a retired Salesforce automation tool. Salesforce Flow is the current platform, supporting screen flows, record-triggered flows, scheduled flows, and autolaunched flows. Flows handle decision logic, loops, batch operations, and error handling. Salesforce recommends migrating all Process Builder automations to Flows.

mainEntity.name: How do I measure data quality in Salesforce?

acceptedAnswer.text: Data quality is measured across five dimensions: completeness (percentage of records with required fields populated, target 95%+), accuracy (verified against source documents, under 5% error rate), consistency (standardized formats across picklist and free-text fields), timeliness (records modified within 18 months), and uniqueness (duplicate records identified via shared identifiers). Each dimension can be tracked using native Salesforce reports. Data quality assessment is a prerequisite for AI feature activation.

mainEntity.name: What is the Salesforce Trust Layer and why does it matter for AI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Trust Layer is a three-phase security architecture between Salesforce data and external AI models. In the Prompt Journey, it performs dynamic grounding and data masking. During Response Generation, masked prompts reach the LLM under zero data retention agreements. In the Response Journey, outputs pass through toxicity detection and de-masking. It prevents data leaks but does not validate AI accuracy, which requires a separate governance framework.

mainEntity.name: What are Salesforce governor limits?

acceptedAnswer.text: Governor limits are hard ceilings on Salesforce's multi-tenant architecture. Synchronous transactions allow 100 SOQL queries, 150 DML statements, and 10 seconds of CPU time. Asynchronous transactions (Batch Apex) reset these limits per chunk with 60 seconds of CPU time. The most common violations come from non-bulkified code and Flows that query inside loops.

mainEntity.name: What is data skew in Salesforce?

acceptedAnswer.text: Data skew occurs when record distribution is heavily imbalanced: one user owns millions of records (ownership skew), one Account has thousands of child records (parent-child skew), or one lookup value is referenced disproportionately (lookup skew). Skew causes record locking failures and timeout errors. Fixes include redistributing records, restructuring data models, and reducing transaction times on parent objects.

mainEntity.name: What is Zero Copy architecture in Salesforce?

acceptedAnswer.text: Zero Copy allows Salesforce to read and write data from external warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks) without physically copying data into the CRM. Data stays in the warehouse and is queried in real time through federated connections. This eliminates ETL pipelines, reduces storage costs, and simplifies compliance by keeping data under its original access controls.

mainEntity.name: When should I use Flow vs Apex for AI agent triggers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Use Flow when automation involves standard CRUD operations, has fewer than 10 decision branches, and will be maintained by admins. Use Apex when logic requires complex data transformations, handles over 10,000 records, needs precise error handling, or interacts with external APIs. If the automation takes more than 15 minutes to explain on the Flow canvas, it probably belongs in Apex.

mainEntity.name: What is Salesforce Einstein and how does it work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Einstein is the AI layer built into Salesforce, including predictive scoring, natural language processing, recommendation engines, and generative AI (Copilot and Agentforce). Predictions require historical data: at least 400 closed-won and 400 closed-lost opportunities for opportunity scoring, or 1,000 leads with conversion data for lead scoring. Data governance is a prerequisite for accurate AI predictions.
